notes: Adds unquoted-brace helpers on Token and uses them consistently across the dispenser and parser, including NextArg/NextBlock, directive(), blockTokens, doImport, openCurlyBrace and closeCurlyBrace; the tests are solid (dispenser, parser, and an adapt integration test), but the helpers were inserted between Quoted()'s doc comment and its func, which detaches that comment, and it leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check plus one inconsistent inline Quoted() check in addresses().

Fixes the root cause by adding `isOpenBrace` and `isCloseBrace` helpers that skip quoted tokens, applied consistently across the dispenser and parser (`NextArg`, `NextBlock`, `directive`, `blockTokens`, `doImport`, open/close checks), with good unit and integration tests; however, the helpers were inserted between `Quoted()` and its doc comment, which detaches that comment, and the `wasQuoted == 0` check in `directive()` is now redundant dead logic.

Changing the map value to a slice of import statements fixes the reported single-module for_each case cleanly. But the parent-override rule still works per ConfigResource: if a parent module imports any instance, child-module blocks for other instances are dropped without warning, the same class of silent loss the issue reports. This likely explains failing 2 of 3 hidden tests, and the added test covers only the basic root-module scenario.

Fixes the root cause by keeping a slice of import statements per ConfigResource, so multiple blocks in the same module are all honored. The parent-overrides-child rule stays at ConfigResource level: a parent block for one instance still silently drops a child's blocks for other instances. The changed public return type likely explains the hidden-test failures, and only one integration test was added, with no unit test for FindImportStatements.

Adds `--once` to the shared option flag set, so it reaches run, cloud and archive. It rejects shortcut flags and applies the rewrite right after consolidation and before derive: one shared-iterations 1/1 scenario keeping exec, env, tags and options, with top-level shortcuts cleared and multiple scenarios rejected. Minor nits: the intermediate BaseConfig copy is awkward, an unset exec becomes an explicit 'default', and env-var shortcuts (K6_VUS etc.) are not guarded. Unit and end-to-end tests are solid.

Adds `--once` to the shared option flag set and rejects it alongside shortcut flags. The scenario transform runs after config consolidation, so `run`, `cloud run` and `archive` all pick it up. It errors on multiple scenarios and rebuilds a single shared-iterations 1/1 scenario that keeps exec, env, tags and options. Unit and end-to-end tests are thorough. Minor nits: the intermediate `base` struct is roundabout, `exec` is always set explicitly to "default", and shortcut values coming from env vars are silently discarded rather than rejected.

Correctly builds a slug-aware section path from the ancestor chain and applies it to section, taxonomy and term pages and to all descendant pages, with a good multilingual test; but `append` on the cached `Ancestors().Reverse()` slice risks shared-slice mutation, and normalized path segments can diverge from unnormalized ones when `disablePathToLower` is set.

Rebuilds the section path from ancestor slugs and substitutes it into the section base and container dir, which correctly covers sections, nested descendants, taxonomies and terms; however, unslugged segments use the normalized (lowercased) path even when disablePathToLower is set, `:sections` permalink tokens ignore slugs, and the ancestor chain is recomputed for every page; the focused integration test covers the issue example plus subsection, taxonomy and term cases.

Fixes the round-trip by wrapping a parenthesised `*NumberLiteral` in a synthetic unary-plus `*DurationExpr` with `Wrapped` set. The grammar and generated parser are updated consistently, and the parse-time zero checks look through the wrapper via `durationNumberLiteral`. It is a somewhat hacky AST encoding that turns plain literals into `OriginalOffsetExpr`/`RangeExpr`. Cases like `foo[-(5)]` or `4d / -(0)` are no longer caught at parse time and only fail at evaluation. Tests are solid across printer, parse-error and promqltest.

Fixes the round-trip by wrapping a parenthesised literal in a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr (Op ADD, nil LHS) and teaches the positive and div/mod-zero checks to look through it, though that sentinel encoding is somewhat hacky. Negated forms in duration_expr context, such as `foo[-(5s)]` or `x / -(0)`, now produce SUB-wrapped nodes the helper does not see through, so their validation moves from parse time to evaluation time. Tests are thorough: printer round-trips, updated AST expectations, new parse-error cases and promqltest evaluation cases.

The sentinel `ReturnError` approach matches the issue and drops the old wrapper transform, but there are four problems: half the hidden tests and the package suite fail; a bare `return` in a partial yields nil instead of the documented `template.HTML("")`; a `return` inside a `{{ template }}`/`define` aborts the whole outer template; and the candidate rewrote an existing test's expected error message to fit its new behavior.

The sentinel-error approach matches the issue: a panic is trapped in exec, the old wrapper transform is removed, and the value is extracted in doInclude. However, a `return` inside a `define`/`template` block will terminate the entire outer template, a bare `return` now yields nil instead of the documented empty `template.HTML`, the `moveReturnLast` pipeline rewrite is a hack, an existing test's assertion was changed to fit the new behavior, and the hidden tests only half pass with the package suite failing.
